scope: Candidate scan and static inspection of node-layout matches in the runtime analysis snapshot; subdivision builder remains unidentified.
method: Stream Capstone over the first executable section in four independently guarded slices. Identify candidates touching the same register at both node facet-range offsets and at least three bound offsets. Decompile four filtered candidates using isolated Ghidra.
findings: 0x140213e90 and 0x1403999e0 are recursive nearest-face search routines with the same child and leaf-range layout, using float and double query inputs respectively.
0x14082d4d0 is a recursive query routine, not established as a builder.
0x14089cb10 uses similar tree bounds and children for a different point-oriented query; its input is not shown to be the Split facet tree.
The filtered candidates do not establish subdivision or tree population.
limitations: Chunk boundaries can begin within instructions, so this heuristic scan can miss functions; matching offsets do not establish object identity.
Register filtering excludes stack/frame-pointer bases and optimized writes; builder code may use helpers or different offset patterns.
The initial unchunked disassembly failed with a 4,295,245,824-byte peak and cleaned up; a chunked unsliced attempt timed out at 94,572,544 bytes and cleaned up. Neither produced search results.
No new live native behavior, application behavior, GUI/MCP parity, or Split parity was established.
